units.name: Art Vocabulary & Analysis

concepts.intro: The formal elements are the basic visual building blocks artists combine to construct any image or object.
b: Line: the path of a moving point; can be contour, gestural, implied, or hatching
Shape (2D, flat) vs. Form (3D, volume) — e.g. a circle is a shape, a sphere is a form
Color: defined by hue, value (lightness/darkness), and saturation/intensity
Texture: actual (tactile, e.g. impasto) vs. implied (visual illusion of texture)
Space: positive space (subject) vs. negative space (surrounding area), and depth cues like overlapping and atmospheric perspective
Value: the range of light to dark used to create volume and contrast (chiaroscuro)

concepts.intro: Principles of design describe how the formal elements are organized within a composition to create unity and impact.
b: Balance: symmetrical, asymmetrical, and radial arrangements of visual weight
Emphasis: a focal point created through contrast, placement, or color
Movement: the path the eye follows through a composition, often via line or repetition
Rhythm and Repetition: repeated elements that create visual tempo
Proportion and Scale: the relative size of forms to each other and to the human body
Unity and Variety: the balance between a cohesive whole and enough contrast to stay interesting

concepts.intro: Understanding the physical processes and materials artists use is essential to reading how a work was made.
b: Fresco: pigment applied to wet plaster (buon fresco) so it bonds as the wall dries, used by Michelangelo in the Sistine Chapel
Oil painting: pigment suspended in oil, allowing slow drying, blending, and glazing, pioneered in the Netherlands by Jan van Eyck
Sculpture in the round vs. relief (bas-relief/low relief and alto-relief/high relief)
Printmaking: woodcut (relief), engraving/etching (intaglio), and lithography (planographic)
Contrapposto: a sculptural pose with weight shifted onto one leg, creating a naturalistic S-curve
Chiaroscuro and tenebrism: strong light-dark contrast used by Caravaggio to create drama

concepts.intro: Formal analysis is the systematic description of what is visible in a work before interpreting its meaning.
b: Step 1 — Description: identify subject matter, medium, and scale without interpretation
Step 2 — Formal elements: analyze line, color, composition, and space
Step 3 — Context: consider patron, date, and original location/function
Step 4 — Interpretation: connect form to meaning, iconography, and historical context
Iconography is the study of symbolic content (e.g., a lily symbolizing purity in Annunciation scenes)
Provenance traces a work's ownership history and authenticates attribution

concepts.intro: Art is commonly grouped by genre, which historically implied a hierarchy of prestige.
b: History painting: depictions of historical, mythological, or religious narratives, ranked highest in the Academic hierarchy
Portraiture: representation of a specific individual, often signaling status through attributes
Landscape: depiction of natural scenery, elevated to fine art status in the 17th-century Dutch Golden Age
Still life: arrangements of inanimate objects, often carrying symbolic (vanitas) meaning
Genre painting: scenes of everyday life, common in 17th-century Dutch art (e.g., Vermeer)
The Académie's hierarchy of genres placed history painting above portrait, genre, landscape, and still life

concepts.intro: Art historically served specific patrons and functions rather than existing purely for aesthetic display.
b: The Catholic Church was the dominant patron of Medieval and Renaissance art, commissioning altarpieces and frescoes
Wealthy families like the Medici in Florence funded civic and religious commissions to display power
Guilds and confraternities commissioned works for chapels and public buildings
Royal courts (e.g., Louis XIV at Versailles) used art to project political authority
The rise of the art market and independent collectors in the 19th century reduced reliance on single patrons

keyFacts: Value contrast (chiaroscuro) creates the illusion of three-dimensional volume on a flat surface.
The Académie's genre hierarchy ranked history painting above portrait, genre, landscape, and still life.
Contrapposto, first mastered in ancient Greek sculpture, was revived by Renaissance sculptors like Donatello.
Iconographic symbols (lilies, skulls, mirrors) carry culturally specific meanings that change across periods.
traps: Shape is two-dimensional and flat; form is three-dimensional and has volume — they are not interchangeable.
Fresco is painted into wet plaster, not applied to a dry wall like most other painting techniques.
Formal analysis describes what is seen before interpreting meaning; students often skip straight to interpretation and miss visual evidence.
Tenebrism (extreme dark-light contrast with little mid-tone, used by Caravaggio) is a stronger effect than ordinary chiaroscuro, not a synonym for it.

quiz.q: Which pair correctly distinguishes shape from form?
o: Shape is 2D and flat; form is 3D and has volume
Shape and form both mean three-dimensional volume
Shape refers only to color; form refers to line
Shape and form are interchangeable terms
quiz.e: Shape describes a flat, two-dimensional area, while form describes a three-dimensional volume such as a sphere or cube.

quiz.q: What is the primary characteristic of buon fresco painting?
o: Pigment is applied to wet plaster and bonds as it dries
Pigment is mixed with egg yolk on wood panels
Pigment is suspended in oil for slow drying
Pigment is fired onto ceramic surfaces
quiz.e: Buon fresco requires paint to be applied while the plaster is still wet so the pigment becomes chemically bonded to the wall as it cures.

quiz.q: Contrapposto refers to which sculptural feature?
o: A pose with weight shifted onto one leg, creating a natural S-curve
The use of negative space around a figure
A technique for casting bronze in sections
quiz.e: Contrapposto is the naturalistic weight-shift pose first perfected in ancient Greek sculpture and revived in the Renaissance.

quiz.q: In the Académie's traditional hierarchy of genres, which category ranked highest?
quiz.e: History painting, depicting historical, mythological, or religious narratives, was considered the most intellectually demanding and prestigious genre.

quiz.q: What does chiaroscuro describe?
o: The use of strong contrasts between light and dark to model form
The layering of transparent oil glazes
A method of carving marble in high relief
The application of gold leaf to panel paintings
quiz.e: Chiaroscuro is an Italian term meaning 'light-dark,' referring to the use of value contrast to create the illusion of volume.

quiz.q: Which best defines negative space in a composition?
o: The empty or background area surrounding the主要 subject
The darkest values in a painting
The outline defining a subject's edge
The area of highest color saturation
quiz.e: Negative space is the area around and between the main subjects of an image, which itself shapes the composition.

quiz.q: Tenebrism, associated with Caravaggio, is best described as:
o: An extreme use of dark-light contrast with little mid-tone transition
A pastel technique for soft blending
A method of underpainting in grisaille
A style of loose, visible brushwork
quiz.e: Tenebrism pushes chiaroscuro to an extreme, plunging most of the composition into shadow with a sharp beam of light.

quiz.q: Which medium allowed for slow drying time and rich glazing effects, revolutionizing Northern European painting?
quiz.e: Oil paint, refined by Netherlandish painters like Jan van Eyck, dries slowly and allows for layered transparent glazes.

quiz.q: What is iconography in art history?
o: The study of symbolic and narrative content within images
The cataloguing of an artist's complete works
The measurement of a painting's physical dimensions
quiz.e: Iconography interprets the symbols, subjects, and themes embedded in a work, such as a lily representing purity.

quiz.q: A relief sculpture that projects only slightly from its background is called:
quiz.e: Bas-relief, or low relief, has figures that project only slightly from the flat background surface.

quiz.q: Which best describes 'provenance' in art history?
o: The documented ownership history of a work of art
The specific brand of pigment used
The size ratio between a work and its frame
The genre classification of a painting
quiz.e: Provenance traces the chain of ownership of a work, which helps establish authenticity and value.

quiz.q: Symmetrical balance in a composition means:
o: Visual weight is evenly distributed on either side of a central axis
All elements radiate from a central point
The image uses only primary colors
The composition has no discernible focal point
quiz.e: Symmetrical balance mirrors visual weight across a central axis, often used in religious altarpieces for solemnity.

quiz.q: What distinguishes intaglio printmaking (engraving, etching) from relief printmaking (woodcut)?
o: In intaglio, ink sits in recessed lines; in relief, ink sits on raised surfaces
Intaglio uses only wood; relief uses only metal
Intaglio prints cannot be reproduced multiple times
Relief printing requires an acid bath
quiz.e: Intaglio processes cut or etch lines into a metal plate that hold ink, while relief processes like woodcut ink the raised surface.

quiz.q: A vanitas still life typically symbolizes:
o: The transience of life and inevitability of death
Political allegiance to a royal court
The wealth of a trading guild
Religious devotion to a specific saint
quiz.e: Vanitas paintings use symbols like skulls, snuffed candles, and wilting flowers to remind viewers of mortality.

quiz.q: Which term describes the path the viewer's eye follows through a composition?
quiz.e: Movement, a principle of design, guides the eye across a work using line, contrast, and repetition.

quiz.q: Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel ceiling was executed using which technique?
quiz.e: Michelangelo painted the ceiling in true fresco, applying pigment to wet plaster in sections called giornate.

quiz.q: Which Renaissance patron family is most associated with funding Florentine art and architecture?
quiz.e: The Medici, a powerful banking family, funded major commissions by artists such as Botticelli and Michelangelo.

quiz.q: What best defines 'atmospheric perspective'?
o: A technique using color and clarity shifts to suggest depth, with distant objects appearing hazier and bluer
A method of overlapping shapes to hide background details
A grid system used to scale up preparatory drawings
The layering of varnish to protect a finished painting
quiz.e: Atmospheric (aerial) perspective mimics how the atmosphere softens and cools the color of distant objects.

quiz.q: Genre painting, as a category, depicts:
quiz.e: Genre painting captures ordinary domestic or social scenes, exemplified by 17th-century Dutch artists like Vermeer and Steen.

quiz.q: The 'formal analysis' method in art history begins with which step?
o: Objective description of subject matter, medium, and scale
quiz.e: Formal analysis starts with unbiased description before moving to formal elements, context, and interpretation.

quiz.q: Which best describes 'implied line'?
o: A line suggested by the alignment of separate elements rather than an actual drawn line
A line created using a ruler and compass
A line used exclusively in printmaking
quiz.e: Implied lines are perceived by the viewer through the arrangement of shapes, gazes, or gestures rather than being physically drawn.

quiz.q: Hue, value, and saturation together define which formal element?
quiz.e: Hue (the color itself), value (lightness/darkness), and saturation (intensity) are the three properties that define color.

quiz.q: A 'focal point' in a composition is created primarily through:
o: Contrast, placement, or unique color that draws the eye
quiz.e: Emphasis, or a focal point, is achieved by making one area stand out through contrast in value, color, or position.

quiz.q: Sculpture 'in the round' is defined as:
o: A freestanding three-dimensional work viewable from all sides
A sculpture carved into a flat wall
A sculpture made only of bronze
A miniature model used for study
quiz.e: Sculpture in the round is fully three-dimensional and detached from a background, unlike relief sculpture.

quiz.q: Radial balance arranges elements:
o: Around a central point, like spokes on a wheel
quiz.e: Radial balance organizes visual elements so they radiate outward from a central focus, common in rose windows.

quiz.q: The term 'impasto' refers to:
o: Thickly applied paint that creates visible texture and brushstrokes
A thin, transparent layer of oil glaze
A technique for polishing marble smooth
A method of mixing pigment with egg tempera
quiz.e: Impasto describes paint applied so thickly that it retains ridges and brushstroke texture, seen in works by Van Gogh.

quiz.q: Which best distinguishes 'actual texture' from 'implied texture'?
o: Actual texture can be physically felt; implied texture is a visual illusion created through technique
Actual texture only appears in sculpture
Implied texture only appears in printmaking
quiz.e: Actual texture is tactile on the artwork's surface, while implied texture uses shading and detail to suggest a surface quality that isn't really there.

quiz.q: A patron commissioning an altarpiece in the 15th century was most likely which type of institution or individual?
o: The Catholic Church or a wealthy family funding a chapel
quiz.e: Church institutions and wealthy patrons commissioned altarpieces to decorate chapels and demonstrate piety and status.

quiz.q: What is the primary purpose of a preparatory drawing or 'cartoon' in fresco painting?
o: To transfer a design onto the wet plaster before painting
To serve as the final exhibited artwork
quiz.e: A cartoon, a full-scale preparatory drawing, was pricked or incised to transfer the composition onto fresh plaster.

quiz.q: Rhythm in a composition is created through:
o: Repetition of elements that establishes a visual tempo
The absence of any repeated forms
The use of only cool colors
quiz.e: Rhythm relies on repeated visual elements, similar to a beat in music, to create a sense of consistent movement.

quiz.q: Which statement about proportion and scale is accurate?
o: Proportion concerns relative size relationships among parts of a composition
Scale and proportion are unrelated to composition
Proportion refers exclusively to color mixing
quiz.e: Proportion describes how parts relate in size to each other and the whole, while scale often measures against the human body.

quiz.q: The term 'unity' in design principles refers to:
o: A sense of cohesion among the elements of a composition
The use of a single color only
The physical size of the canvas
quiz.e: Unity is achieved when the elements of a work feel like they belong together, often balanced against variety for interest.

quiz.q: A lithograph is created using which printmaking process?
o: A planographic process using a flat stone or plate treated with grease and water
Carving a design into a wood block
Etching lines into metal with acid
Pressing wet clay into a mold
quiz.e: Lithography works on the principle that grease and water repel each other, allowing ink to adhere only to the drawn image on a flat surface.

quiz.q: Portraiture in art history often functioned to:
o: Signal the sitter's status, wealth, or identity through attributes and dress
quiz.e: Portraits frequently included symbolic objects and clothing to communicate the sitter's rank, profession, or virtues.

quiz.q: Which best describes the function of a 'guild' in the production of Renaissance art?
o: A professional association that trained artists and regulated commissions
A religious order devoted only to prayer
quiz.e: Guilds, such as painters' guilds, trained apprentices, set quality standards, and often awarded commissions.

quiz.q: The Dutch Golden Age elevated which two genres to major status alongside history painting?
quiz.e: In the 17th-century Dutch Republic, without strong church patronage, landscape and still life painting flourished for private buyers.

quiz.q: Which best explains 'variety' as a design principle?
o: The inclusion of diverse elements to prevent a composition from feeling monotonous
The complete absence of any repeated shapes
quiz.e: Variety introduces difference and contrast, balancing unity so a composition remains visually engaging.

quiz.q: A 'giornata' in fresco painting refers to:
o: The section of plaster an artist could complete in a single day's work
A specific pigment made from crushed lapis lazuli
A type of preparatory sketch on paper
The varnish applied after a fresco dries
quiz.e: Because plaster dries quickly, fresco painters worked in daily sections called giornate, visible as seams in some frescoes.

quiz.q: Asymmetrical balance achieves equilibrium by:
o: Balancing visually unequal elements through contrast in size, color, or placement
Mirroring identical shapes on both sides
Placing all elements in the center
quiz.e: Asymmetrical balance uses varied elements of differing visual weight to create equilibrium without mirror symmetry.

quiz.q: Which best describes the relationship between line quality and gesture drawing?
o: Gesture drawing uses quick, loose lines to capture movement and overall pose rather than fine detail
Gesture drawing requires slow, precise contour lines
Gesture drawing is only used in sculpture
Gesture drawing eliminates the use of line entirely
quiz.e: Gesture drawings prioritize capturing energy and the essential pose of a subject with rapid, fluid marks.
